subject: Billing units Q&A: tokens vs characters, caching effects
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia.vega@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + follow-ups from today's pricing chat (tokens vs chars + caching)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size a cost estimate and proposal: 

1) What you told us (high level):
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant used inside Acme Health clinician portal.
- Expected volume: roughly 3–5M user-facing requests/month initially (you mentioned pilot-scale 100k/week).
- Engineering currently measures payloads in characters and requests, not tokens.
- Preliminary budget range you gave: $10k–$30k/mo. You also mentioned a target of about $20 per 1M tokens for planning math (is that target or a guess?).

2) Clarify please: (answers will let us provide an apples-to-apples estimate)
- For a typical request, what is the average prompt length in characters? (if you only have examples, send 10 representative samples)
- Do you expect many prompts to be identical or templated such that caching (prefix or full response caching) will meaningfully reduce model calls?
- Target SLA / latency requirement for in-app responses? (we'll use this to choose model variants)

3) How we bill and what to expect (short):
- Redwood billing is token-based: billed tokens = prompt tokens + completion tokens (there's no separate "per request" metric that replaces tokens).
- Tokens are different from characters — rough conversion rules in my next email.
- If you cache responses at the app layer and avoid calling the model, those calls are not billed. If you call the model and we can reuse KV cache across steps, that's an implementation optimization but still results in billed tokens for the new model compute.

Attached: pricing_model_comparison.xlsx (quick sketch of sample unit economics).

Next steps: please send 8–12 sample prompts (or a representative CSV) and confirm the monthly target range we should model to return a 3-scenario (pilot / expected / scale) cost estimate. Diego can draft the technical notes on caching/token mapping.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Recap + follow-ups from today's pricing chat (tokens vs chars + caching)

Hi Karthik — great summary, thanks. A few answers and a quick question on what's billed: 

- Average prompt length: our analytics team reports about 1,100–1,800 characters for user prompts (the triage template expands with some context each time). I attached a small sample file (request_sample.txt) with 12 anonymized prompts.
- Caching: we can cache exact prompts/responses for the most common flows (top 10 templates) but many prompts are slightly different (patient notes appended), so effective cache hit rate probably will be ~15–25% initially.
- Monthly volume: pilot (0.4M), expected (4M), scale (12M) requests. Note: these are requests, not tokens — happy to have you convert.
- Budget: our procurement team indicated a target spend band of $10k–$30k/month for this service line. We were using a blunt target of $20 per 1M tokens as a planning figure — not a firm requirement.

Question on billing: our infra team counts characters (for legacy reasons) and wants to understand how tokens translate and whether cached prompts will still count toward billed tokens. If caching avoids a call to the model, I understand it won't be billed — but if we have partial prompt reuse (shared intro + variable tail), will that still be billed as full prompt tokens?

Also cc'ing Tom Li (our eng lead) for any follow-ups.

Best,
Alicia Vega
Product Lead, Clinical AI | Acme Health
Alicia.Vega@acmehealth.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia.vega@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 13:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + follow-ups from today's pricing chat (tokens vs chars + caching)

Hi Alicia — quick technical clarifications that should help convert your "chars/requests" to billed tokens and understand caching behavior. TL;DR: billed tokens = tokens(prompt) + tokens(completion). Caching can avoid model calls (no billing) but if you call the model you will be billed for the tokens sent/returned.

1) Characters -> tokens (rule of thumb):
- For English text, a conservative conversion is ~4 characters per token (so 1,200 chars ≈ 300 tokens). With lots of punctuation or code, the ratio changes. Using your sample prompts I ran a spot-conversion: your 12 prompts average ~1,350 chars ≈ 330 tokens.

2) What counts as billed tokens:
- If your app submits the entire prompt to Redwood, we bill for the prompt tokens you send plus the tokens in the model completion.
- If you use prefix/prompt caching at your app layer and skip the model call entirely for a cache hit, there is no billed token usage for that request.
- Partial reuse: if you still call the model (for example you de-duplicate a static instruction prefix but append variable patient notes and still invoke the model), you will be billed for the tokens in whatever text you actually send in the request (prefix + variable). There is no automatic "pro-rated" billing discount for reused prefixes unless you avoid the call or use an internal caching proxy that returns a stored response without hitting the model.

3) KV cache and session reuse (for multi-turn flows):
- KV cache is an optimization for latency and memory; it reduces repeated computation for the transformer when the same KV pairs are reused across calls on the same session. However, each new model call still consumes/produces tokens that are counted against billing unless the result is served from an app-level cache.

4) Sample unit economics — approximate (use your numbers to recalc):
- Example: expected scenario = 4M requests/month, avg prompt 330 tokens, avg completion 150 tokens -> tokens per request = 480 tokens.
- Total tokens = 4,000,000 * 480 = 1,920,000,000 tokens (~1.92B tokens).
- If target price is $20 per 1M tokens: cost = (1,920M tokens / 1M) * $20 = $38,400/month.
- If you can cache 20% of requests (no model call), billed tokens drop to 1.536B -> $30,720/mo.

5) Practical suggestions:
- Send us a CSV of example prompts and an estimate of expected completion length per flow; we'll run a quick tokenization pass and return a 3-scenario cost table (pilot/expected/scale) using Redwood's recommended model variants and caching assumptions.
- Consider server-side response caching for the deterministic templates to avoid billed model calls entirely.
- If latency is strict (<250ms), we'll size for a lower-latency instance class which can change unit price; we'll call that out explicitly in the estimate.

Happy to run the tokenization for your 12-sample file and post back numbers. If useful, we can also include an optional short pilot (7–14 days) where we instrument token counts against your traffic to produce real observed economics.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
